item.title: Troubleshoot HTTP 404 Not Found: URL, Routes, Paths and Server Config
item.description:
An HTTP 404 response normally means that the requested resource could not be found. The following checks cover some of the most common causes.

  1. Incorrect URL: Verify the complete URL, including its path and filename, and check carefully for spelling mistakes.

  2. Missing resource: If you requested a file, confirm that it exists at the specified server location. For dynamic content, make sure the corresponding endpoint or route exists.

  3. Permission or access rules: Some servers deliberately return 404 instead of 403 for resources that the current user is not allowed to discover. Check authentication and access-control settings.

  4. Server configuration: Review document roots, rewrite rules, route configuration, deployment paths, and file permissions.

  5. Letter case: File paths are case-sensitive on many servers. Make sure the capitalization in the URL exactly matches the deployed filename.

  6. Network or proxy behavior: Confirm that the request reaches the expected server. A proxy, CDN, gateway, or incorrect host configuration may send it somewhere else.

  7. Server-side failure or incomplete deployment: If the URL and route are correct, check whether the required service is running and whether all files were deployed successfully.

  8. URL encoding: Special characters in a URL must be encoded correctly. Incorrect encoding can cause the server to interpret the path differently.
